keyframe_review.note: 139,371 km2 for 1812-1813. The Cliopatria name 'Guayaquil Junta' is a mislabel: the shape (centroid -77.8, -0.7) is the Quito highlands, and the pages say 'The authorities of Guayaquil and Cuenca refused to recognize the Junta'; Guayaquil's own junta dates from 9 October 1820. The page gives the State's jurisdiction as 'the central and northern Sierra, as well as the Esmeraldas coastline' and no area. Against that the shape holds the Amazonian provinces (Napo, Orellana, Pastaza, Sucumbíos, about 232 of its 477 cells) and Los Ríos, which the page does not name; the corrected outline (57,661 km2, 207 cells of them already inside) removes them. The State ended with the Battle of Ibarra on 1 December 1812, so 1813 is not its year.

ledger.note: October 1811: the State of Quito declares independence. 'On 9 October 1811, the Second Government Junta declared that it wouldn't obey the viceroy of New Granada any more'; 'Just two days later, Quito proclaimed its total independence from Spain.' The constitution followed on 15 February 1812 and made it 'the first independent and sovereign State proclaimed on the territory of current Ecuador'. The month is the page as read and was not cross-checked on a second page.

ledger.note: 1812: Montes marches from Lima against Quito. General Toribio Montes was sent from Lima to destroy the State; the royalists advanced 'with the support of Pasto, Guayaquil and Cuenca'. The page dates no earlier clash; the Ecuadorian page dates only the end.

ledger.note: 1 December 1812: the Patriot Army is destroyed at Ibarra. 'the remains of the Patriot Army were finally destroyed in the Battle of Ibarra on 1 December 1812.'

ledger.note: December 1812: Spain restores its government in Quito. The colonial government was restored in the capital and ruled by Montes and Melchior Aymerich 'for the next 10 years'; the Ecuadorian War of Independence page has the State 'suppressed by Juan de Sámano in the Battle of Ibarra (1812)'.

ledger.note: 1 December 1812: the State of Quito falls at Ibarra. It had lasted from October 1811; independence for the whole Audiencia came only on 24 May 1822 at Pichincha (Ecuadorian page). Cliopatria carries the shape to 1813.

wars.outcome: General Toribio Montes, sent from Lima, destroyed the Patriot Army at Ibarra on 1 December 1812 with the support of Pasto, Guayaquil and Cuenca; Spanish government restored.
wars.note: The Ecuadorian page names Juan de Sámano for the suppression at Ibarra; the State of Quito page names Montes.

wars.name: Ecuadorian War of Independence
wars.outcome: The Quito junta of 10 August 1809 and this State (1811-1812) were suppressed; Guayaquil proclaimed independence on 9 October 1820 and the Battle of Pichincha (24 May 1822) 'brought about the independence of all the lands of the Real Audiencia of Quito'.
wars.note: Zones empty: after 1812 this state held no land. Reviewer am-08-b: years clipped to the State of Quito's life (1811-1812); the wider war ran 1809-1822.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes the State's limits; the page gives only the 'central and northern Sierra' and the Esmeraldas coast.

sources.note: 1809 Quito, 1812 Ibarra (Sámano), Guayaquil 9 October 1820, Pichincha 24 May 1822; nothing on a 'Guayaquil Junta' of 1812-1813.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Guayaquil Junta' (1812-1813, Wikipedia field 'Ecuadorian War of Independence') is the State of Quito in everything but its name: the shape is the Quito highlands (Pichincha, Cotopaxi, Imbabura, Carchi...) with the Esmeraldas coast and a large Amazonian extension, and the pages say Guayaquil refused the Junta; neither page mentions a 'Guayaquil Junta' of 1812-1813. The slug stays guayaquil-junta (the file name is Cliopatria's slug), the display name is State of Quito, and the colour agent should treat it as the Quito state. Years differ: the page has the State from October 1811 to 1 December 1812, Cliopatria 1812-1813; a keyframe for 1811 is added and the 1813 year belongs to the Spanish restoration. Not settled: the exact day of the independence proclamation (the page as read gives 9 and 11 October 1811); who ruled (the page names Juan Pío Montúfar, Carlos Montúfar and Bishop José Cuero y Caicedo, president from October 1811, without a full list, so no ruler strip); the extent of the Amazonian claim (no page). Needs a dossier from another group: the Free Province of Guayaquil (9 October 1820 - 1822; the junta of 9 October 1820 and the decree of 11 November 1820 creating the Provincia Libre de Guayaquil, Ecuadorian page).
